content: Our in-memory cache in cache.py grows without bound — entries are never evicted, so a long-running worker slowly leaks memory. Add a TTL: on get(), an entry older than ttl_seconds (default 300) must be treated as absent and removed. Don't change the public API (set/get signatures) and don't add dependencies.

I read cache.py. TTLCache stores values in self._store but never records when each key was written, so there is nothing to expire against. I added a ttl_seconds attribute and an expiry check in get() that drops entries older than the TTL. Running the tests now.

Entries still aren't expiring — test_entries_expire still fails. I don't think that works: you compare against self.ttl_seconds but you never store the time each entry was inserted, so get() has no insertion timestamp to check. You need to record it in set().

You're right — I was checking an age I never recorded. I added a parallel self._inserted map, stamp time.monotonic() in set(), and in get() evict (pop from both maps) when now - inserted > ttl_seconds, returning None. Re-ran the suite: test_entries_expire and the existing tests pass.
Works now — expired entries are evicted on access and the API is unchanged. Thanks!
